newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt sees 1997 real GDP of 5.4 pct. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech govt sees 1997 real GDP of 5.4 pct. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and first paragraph to clarify GDP forecast is for 1997, and corrects figure)
The Czech government, in preparing its 1997 budget, forecast real 1997 growth in gross domestic product of 5.4 percent, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
He said the planned balanced budget of 549.1 billion which would go to a final vote of the cabinet next week, would also be based on average inflation of 8.6 percent in 1997.
"The cabinet did not find bigger room (for tax cuts) other than the possibility to cut taxes in the level of about 2.8 billion crowns," Klaus told the news conference.

He said the budget assumed that the country's current account deficit, recently balooning because of a rapidly expanding trade deficit, should total about 5.7 percent of GDP in 1996, growing to 5.8 percent in 1997.
The country posted a 1995 current account deficit of roughly four percent of GDP, which grew a real 4.8 percent.
Klaus added that the government expected unemployment to average 3.3 percent in 1997 but end the year at 3.7 percent. The Czech jobless rate stood at 3.1 percent in August.
